column1: A model's supported input types, such as text or images, are its {{c1::modalities}}.
column2:
Choose input capabilities that match the data your SQL application needs to process.

column1: Retrieving relevant SQL data and supplying it to a model before generation is {{c1::Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)}}.
column2:
The retrieved data grounds the response in application context rather than only pretrained knowledge.

column1: Learned numeric vectors that represent features or meaning of database content are {{c1::embeddings}}.
column2:
Select a model that supports embedding generation for the type of data being represented.
Review source

column1: Finding meaning-related SQL content by comparing embeddings is {{c1::vector search}}.
column2:
It compares numeric representations rather than requiring exact keyword matches.
Review source

column1: Models process text in units such as word pieces or punctuation called {{c1::tokens}}.
column2:
One word can split into several tokens.

column1: Splitting database text into smaller pieces before embedding is called {{c1::chunking}}.
column2:
Keep each chunk within the embedding model's input token limit.
